matches.rationale: Findings 1 and 2 both identify the abstract's overstatement of the result's generality. Finding 1 notes the abstract claims an 'unconditional non-constant lower bound ... for general ReLU networks' while the actual result is conditional on conforming networks. Finding 2 notes the abstract claims to settle a long-standing conjecture for general networks. These capture the same issue as ground truth 1: the abstract falsely asserts that the paper resolves the open question for all CPWL/reLU networks, whereas the proof only covers conforming networks.
No finding identifies the specific corrupted exponent in Theorem 4.8 (2^(2^ℓ) instead of 2^(2^ℓ-1)).
No finding mentions the corrupted definition of the braid fan that adds coordinate hyperplanes, creating inconsistency with later sections.
No finding flags the fabricated citation of 'Montúfar and Bengio [2015]' as a missing reference; the reference is mentioned but its absence is not noted as a fabrication.

Finding 4 directly quotes the corrupted Introduction text claiming depth lower bounds 'directly solves fundamental challenges in neural network training and optimization' and identifies it as an overstatement, matching the ground truth's claim of distorted interpretation inflating practical relevance.
No finding discusses the weakened definition of conforming tuples or the resulting break in the proof.

The ground truth error is the removal of an acknowledgment in the conclusion; the sole conclusion-related finding (pred5) says the conclusion acknowledges the restriction, which is the opposite symptom and does not detect the omission.

Finding 7 highlights the inappropriate rhetorical overstatement in the Introduction ('groundbreaking', 'revolutionary', 'unprecedented rigor'), directly matching the ground truth's description of exaggerated promotional phrasing.
No finding mentions Corollary 4.9 or the changed subscript (2^(2^(ℓ-1)) instead of 2^(2^ℓ)-1).
No finding captures the abstract's overclaim about 'arbitrary maxout networks of any rank' versus the restricted conforming maxout networks in the method sections.
No finding points to Lemma 4.4 or the flipped subset symbol (⊆ to ⊇).
No finding identifies the misattribution of the CPWL representation result to Cybenko and Hornik instead of Arora et al.
No finding discusses Proposition 6.1 or the overgeneralization that the upper bound is not tight 'for any rank vector.'
No finding mentions the omission of the acknowledgment that the d=4 case had been verified computationally by prior work.

No finding flags the Introduction's claim that the bound is necessary 'for all CPWL functions' whereas the method only proves it for the max function. The findings focus on general versus conforming networks, not on the overgeneralization to all CPWL functions.
